claims.text: High-entropy-alloy design involves a vast compositional space that requires efficient computational screening tools.
CALPHAD has an important role in high-throughput HEA design and screening.
CALPHAD calculations require suitable computational software and thermodynamic databases.
Refractory HEAs generally crystallize as BCC solid solutions and have very high melting points relevant to elevated-temperature applications.
A hybrid CALPHAD, first-principles DFT, and machine-learning methodology is required to predict Tm, entropy of fusion, and heat capacity for multicomponent RHEAs.
Existing refractory-element thermodynamic databases are often incomplete or extrapolated for complex multicomponent configurations.
Incomplete or inaccurate database parameters produce high uncertainty in the liquid-phase description of RHEAs.
DFT-derived formation enthalpies and vibrational free energies can be used to parameterize a CALPHAD liquid-phase model for W-Mo-Ta-Nb-V alloys.
First-principles DFT accurately captures the electronic and vibrational contributions needed for RHEA free-energy calculations.
An ML model trained on limited DFT-CALPHAD data can predict solid- and liquid-phase Gibbs energies across a much larger compositional space.
Melting temperature is obtained from the intersection of the solid and liquid Gibbs-energy curves.
Entropy of fusion is the entropy difference between the liquid and solid at the melting temperature.
Heat capacity can be derived from the temperature derivative of enthalpy.
Configurational entropy and lattice distortion stabilize the BCC solid solution and influence entropy of fusion.
The liquid phase can be represented as a disordered solution with interaction parameters derived from DFT.
The methodology is valid when the high-temperature alloy forms a stable single-phase solid solution or a predictable two-phase mixture.
Strong chemical ordering, complex intermetallic formation, or liquid short-range order outside the training distribution increases prediction error.
The proposed workflow can predict RHEA melting temperatures within ±50 K and entropy of fusion within ±10%.
The proposed workflow reduces computational cost by more than 90% relative to pure DFT phase-diagram calculations.
Standard CALPHAD databases often produce melting-temperature errors greater than 100 K for complex RHEAs.

contradictions.description: The claimed accuracy is ±50 K for Tm and ±10% for ΔSfus, but the method is falsified only beyond ±100 K or ±20%. Results outside the claimed accuracy yet inside the falsification limits would violate the predicted outcome without falsifying the hypothesis.
